topics.title: What Your W-2 Actually Tells You Before You File
topics.angle: Walking through a real, redacted W-2 line by line so a first-time filer knows what each box changes about their refund

audienceIntent.rationale: Directly answers the question first-time filers search for every January: what their own form means.

strategicFit.rationale: Occupies the taxes pillar's declared seasonal emphasis window exactly as planned in the strategy.

differentiation.rationale: Most competing content explains tax rules abstractly; a redacted real-document walkthrough is a distinct format in this category.

timeliness.rationale: Matches the observed category-wide content gap ahead of the January filing season (OBS_TAX_SEASON_GAP).

evergreenPotential.rationale: Relevance is concentrated in the filing season each year; value outside that window is limited.

productionFeasibility.rationale: Fits the long-form duration envelope with one prepared document and no external dependency.

growthPotential.rationale: Seasonal search volume for first-time filing questions extends reach beyond the existing subscriber base.

timelinessWindow.rationale: Matches the channel's declared tax filing season seasonal emphasis and the observed category-wide content gap.

productionConsiderations: Requires a real W-2 form redacted for privacy before filming
Best filmed and published before mid-January to land inside the seasonal window

risks.description: Payroll withholding rules vary by state and require verification before scripting.

topics.title: The Real Cost of Carrying a Balance on One Credit Card
topics.angle: Showing in arithmetic how a minimum payment quietly doubles the price of an ordinary purchase

audienceIntent.rationale: Addresses recurring viewer confusion about minimum payments noted in comment sentiment (OBS_CREDIT_CARD_INTEREST).

strategicFit.rationale: Falls squarely within the budgeting pillar's arithmetic-first mandate.

differentiation.rationale: Framed as a single reproducible calculation rather than generic debt-avoidance advice.

timeliness.rationale: Relevant year-round; no seasonal or news-driven basis was supplied.

evergreenPotential.rationale: The underlying arithmetic does not change with market conditions or the calendar.

productionFeasibility.rationale: A single on-screen amortisation table fits the existing production template with no new assets.

growthPotential.rationale: Addresses a widely searched, category-general question likely to reach new viewers.

productionConsiderations: Needs a clear on-screen amortisation table sourced from the channel's standard calculation template

topics.title: How a Raise Changes Your Take-Home Pay, Step by Step
topics.angle: Tracing a raise through withholding and contribution changes to show the actual increase in a paycheck

audienceIntent.rationale: Answers a question raised naturally by the adjacent negotiation topic already in production.

strategicFit.rationale: Extends the career and income pillar into the arithmetic of a raise's actual effect.

differentiation.rationale: Framed as a step-by-step trace rather than a general statement that raises are taxed at a higher bracket.

timeliness.rationale: Relevant year-round; no seasonal or news-driven basis was supplied.

evergreenPotential.rationale: The mechanism does not depend on current tax-year specifics beyond the bracket structure.

productionFeasibility.rationale: Uses the same paycheck-arithmetic template as prior budgeting content.

growthPotential.rationale: Serves an already-engaged segment more than it reaches new viewers.

risks.description: Marginal tax bracket mechanics are easy to state incorrectly and require careful verification.
